blocks.text:
**Programme year:** 2027

Rio de Janeiro has green hills, blue sky, beautiful bays, islands and marvellous beaches: Brazil’s second-largest city after São Paulo and one of the most beautiful in the world. Copacabana, Ipanema and Leblon are famous for their black-and-white mosaic promenades, and Rio offers almost any sport, from golf, tennis and surfing to diving and hang-gliding. The journey then continues to the Iguazu Falls, to discover their thundering power from both the Brazilian and Argentine sides.

## What you will see in Rio

Private transfer (driver only) from Rio de Janeiro’s Galeão airport to your hotel in Copacabana. Free day.

Day 2 · Corcovado and city tour. Explore Rio’s most famous landmarks, beginning with Christ the Redeemer, one of the New Seven Wonders of the World, with spectacular panoramic views over the city. The tour continues to the colourful Selarón Steps and the Dona Marta lookout, one of Rio’s finest viewpoints, and the impressive Metropolitan Cathedral, with panoramic views of the Sambadrome, home of Rio’s world-famous Carnival parades, and the legendary Maracanã Stadium (both from the outside).

Day 3 · Sugar Loaf. An afternoon at one of Rio’s most iconic landmarks: the famous cable car offers breathtaking panoramic views of the city, Guanabara Bay, the Atlantic Ocean and Rio’s stunning coastline. Afterwards, a scenic drive along Copacabana, Ipanema and Leblon.

A free day to relax and enjoy the city, its beaches and viewpoints. Ask Ada Tours for extra activities: the Botanical Garden, the tropical islands, a sailing tour of Guanabara Bay, a samba and capoeira show or Imperial Petrópolis (see Optional excursions).

## What you will see at Iguazu

Day 5 · Breakfast at the hotel and transfer to the airport for your flight to Foz do Iguaçu; transfer to your hotel. Free day.

Day 6 · An excursion to the Brazilian side of the falls. A calm walk along the edge of the canyon reveals one of the most spectacular views on Earth, with some 275 cascades and rainbows shimmering in the spray, before the path leads to the largest waterfall in the park, the Devil’s Throat, where the water plunges some 80 metres. A walkway takes you into the heart of the falls, surrounded by their power on all sides, before a stairway leads up to look down on them from above. At the end of the tour, your guide drops you off at your hotel (entrance ticket included).

Day 7 · An excursion to the Argentine side of the falls, which is different from the Brazilian one: paths lead you through the falls, giving you the chance to look at them from below and feel the strength of the falling water up close, in a natural park of some 55,500 hectares. Within the park, take the train to the Devil’s Throat, the most powerful of all the falls, and stand directly above the falling water. Tickets included.

## Route and pace

8D / 7N · Rio (4N) · Foz do Iguaçu (3N)

Day 8 · Private transfer (driver only) from the hotel to the airport for your flight home. End of services.

## Travel arrangements

Shared tours in Rio de Janeiro with an English-speaking guide.

Private transfers according to the programme, driver only.

Private Brazilian Falls tour.

Not included: Flight Rio de Janeiro – Foz do Iguaçu

## Price basis

From $ 1,950

Per person, 4★ hotels, sharing a double room. Includes accommodation and services as described.

## Optional excursions

Ask Ada Tours for these extra activities in Rio, bookable on request.

Botanical Garden

A magnificent 137-hectare garden more than 200 years old, with an avenue of 134 royal palms and thousands of plant species: orchids, bromeliads, cacti, giant bamboo, carnivorous plants and the giant Victoria water lily. Monkeys and toucans are often seen.

Tropical islands

Lunch included

From the fishing village of Itacuruçá, in Mangaratiba, about 1.5 hours from Rio, sail across Sepetiba Bay on a saveiro schooner among green tropical islands, with a chance to see dolphins, turtles and parrots, stops to swim and lunch on an island.

Guanabara Bay sailing tour

Discover Rio de Janeiro’s incredible coastline on a beautiful half-day sailing tour.

Samba & capoeira show

An exciting show of Brazilian samba and capoeira by professional dancers, with dinner available during the show and transfers with a guide.

Imperial Petrópolis

A historic mountain town 60 km from Rio, whose land was bought in 1830 by Emperor Pedro I and where Pedro II later built his summer palace, now the Imperial Museum, with the jewelled crown of the emperor; visit the Gothic Cathedral, where Pedro II, Empress Teresa Cristina and Princess Isabel are buried.
